data.plain: Trusting a producer, persona, route, credential or past success where a checker, proof, policy or checked capability should decide.

analogy.boundary: The picture stops at the door; whether the access system itself is right, or how the person behaves inside, is beyond it.

maps.analogy: letting the person in because the face is familiar and the pass looks right
maps.doctrine: trusting a claim because of its producer or credential

maps.analogy: looking the person up in the access system for this room today
maps.doctrine: the independent checker or permission lookup that should decide

maps.analogy: the old pass that worked last time
maps.doctrine: a previous successful run or long-lived credential

analogy.text: A security guard waves someone into a secure room because he recognises their face and they hold an old pass, without looking them up in the access system to see whether they are cleared for that room today.

reader.counterexample: A change to files is allowed because the caller holds a long-lived credential and the same route passed last time, and nothing looks up whether the caller is allowed to make this change now.
reader.does_not_prove: Refusing identity-based trust in these replays leaves open whether the permissions that are granted are correct.

example.text: The tool-authority replay works out whether a tool call is allowed from the capability and policy it looks up, so a known caller with no permission for that call is refused.

reader.governs: Decisions about whether to trust a claim or allow an action.
reader.plain: The mistake of letting something through because of who sent it, what badge it carries or that it worked last time, without checking that this request is allowed right now.
reader.potential_misread: That a trusted name, or a pass that worked before, is a safe substitute for checking this request.
reader.refuses: Trusting a producer, persona, route, credential or past success in place of a checker, proof, policy or a permission looked up for this request.
reader.requires: A small checker that decides each certificate, and permission for each action worked out from current tokens, policy and proof references.
reader.why_it_matters: Identities can be faked or go out of date, and when that happens a system that trusts the sender has nothing checking the request.
